BREAKING: US equity ETFs have attracted +$1.4 trillion in inflows over the last 12 months, their largest 12-month inflow on record.

Tech funds alone have attracted +$65 billion, more than double the inflows into cyclical equity ETFs.

At the same time, defensive equity ETFs have drawn +$25 billion.

In the preceding 12-month period, US equity ETFs attracted +$850 billion.

By comparison, during years 1 and 2 of the current bull market, inflows totaled +$300 billion and +$650 billion, respectively.

Investors are piling into US equity funds at a record pace.

BREAKING: The US deficit widened to $1.99 trillion for FY2026, up +12% from the $1.78 trillion recorded last year.

Spending rose by +6%, to $7.4 trillion, and NET interest officially rose above $1 trillion.

Debt servicing costs are now their third largest expense for the US government, only behind Social Security and Medicare.

This marks the fourth-straight year with the US fiscal deficit around $2 trillion.

The deficit spending crisis is out of control.

BREAKING: The 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, has attracted +$3.8 billion in inflows so far this week, putting it on track for its largest weekly intake on record.

This follows 3 consecutive weekly outflows, the longest streak since May.

By comparison, the previous record weekly inflow was +$3.1 billion posted in June this year.

This comes despite $SOXL falling -35% over the last 7 trading sessions.  

Meanwhile, the Semiconductor ETF, $SMH, has posted +$430 million in inflows so far this week, on track for its biggest weekly inflow since the start of September.

At the same time, the Semiconductor ETF, $SOXX, has attracted +$574 million, on pace for its 2nd-largest weekly intake since August.

Investors are piling into leveraged semiconductor ETFs at a record pace.

Gold and Bitcoin both remain in holding patterns. Below is gold, which has seen steady inflows but continues to be held down by a deceleration in global liquidity growth (per the tightening in financial conditions mentioned earlier). https://t.co/IYrjeOvTCf

Semiconductor stocks are experiencing a historic losing streak:

The Semiconductor Index, $SOX, has declined for 7 consecutive trading sessions, matching its longest streak since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

Over this span, the index has dropped -12.4% erasing -$2 trillion in market value.

This also marks its 5th correction of at least -10.0% this year.

Currently, more than 50% of SOX’s constituents are down at least -10% from their respective highs.

Over the last 20 years, there have only been 2 longer such streaks, in 2006 and 2008.

Semiconductor stocks are seeing massive swings.

What narrative will drive Bitcoin's incoming bull run?

It's a good question, and it's the one I've been asked most often since starting this language analysis work.

One defining characteristic of a bear market is that hope is gone. The stories that drove bull-market euphoria are now absent in the apathy of the bear.

People desperately want a new narrative to latch onto.

They want a reason to be bullish again.

They want a new story to tell.

So now that we are (IMO) in the disbelief stages of this bull market, are any new narratives and stories starting to take shape?

That's exactly what I went searching for this week.

When investing with the mindset of Buy and Hold, most are thinking of Warren Buffett. 

Do you know how many positions Warren Buffett had to write off? 

Do you have the funds and capital inflow to seed new ideas that might end up the next APPLE?

My favorite crowd in the investment world are the "buy and hold" guys.

Buy and hold what? $AAPL ? $NKE? 

First, Buy and Hold strategy is built on survivorship bias.

Second, if you are getting involved in liquid assets marked to market at every minute, you should have the flexibility to receive your cash and move on. 

If you are under water by 50% and waiting for the stock to recover 100% to go breakeven in the long run, maybe stock market is not the place to be.
